title: Belmont singers: Mabel Richardson, Alice Jackson, Teddy Peters
summary: He names the singers at the Belmont and says Old Man Brown gave him his start.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: What was the name of this place, again?
Belmont. That was on the corner of North Carolina and Mediterranean Avenue.
Do you remember any of the singers there, who they were?

Yes, there was a woman called Mabel Richardson. She was from Washington or Baltimore. She was very good. And there was another one named Alice Jackson, I think, yeah, Alice Jackson. And there was nobody, of course, the ones that you would know more than her, but she was working more with Madison Reed, but that was Mary Stafford, she was with him. Mabel Richardson was almost as good as Mary Stafford, though. And there was another woman called Teddy Peters from out in Chicago, I mean, out along the coast. I asked when I was with Rae, And I remember, once I asked this woman, the Peters Sisters in Paris, did they have a relative named -- but they said she wasn't any kin to them, but she looked just like the Peters Sisters. She was big, just like they are, and all. And so, she was up there. And then, well
I had an eye for her for somehow, but she didn't have no eye for me and she said, "Go on, boy, you don't know what you're talking about."

Anyhow, because, I always carried my sex along with my music, because I think that's one thing that made me be a piano player, so that there wouldn't be so many that refused me. At the time, it bothered me. If I was a piano player, they said, "Well, let's give him a break."
I got a break in a lot of places that it wasn't expected.
Well, that's what happened there. So, we did alright there. And from then on, I was on my way. That's where I got my start. When this man gave me my start, Old Man Brown.
